prompt:
Use case: style-transfer and character refinement.
User feedback to incorporate together: restore the BUTTERFLY feeling; make the character much gentler, prettier and cuter as a youthful chibi girl; replace the assertive pose with a delicate feminine standing pose. Keep the project's compact proportions, simplified painted drawing and three-quarter LEFT facing.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1 = original character's silver hair, paired horns, violet palette and especially the SOFT ROUND BUTTERFLY SLEEVE SILHOUETTE and blue/lavender wing markings. Use its costume motifs, not its adult body proportions or outfit exposure.
Image 2 = current revision to change. Its large head/compact body is useful, but its aggressive narrow eyes, sharp eyebrows, claw-like casting hand, wide legs and jagged pointed sleeves are all rejected.
Image 3 = project body-proportion and broad cartoon shape reference ONLY. Do not copy the male archer's clothes, weapons, face, stern eyebrows or pose.
Image 4 = project drawing style: thick natural deep-ink outline, only a few broad matte painted value planes, restrained visible brushwork.

DRAW ONE NEW FINISHED FULL-BODY VERSION:
A very cute, gentle, pretty youthful chibi butterfly mage girl, approximately three actual head heights tall excluding horns. Large softly rounded head, small compact torso, short proportional legs and small hands. Her face has soft rounded cheeks, a tiny nose, large kind lavender cartoon eyes with simple flat iris design, softly curved eyebrows, relaxed eyelids and a small warm closed-mouth smile. Friendly, shyly graceful expression, never smug or fierce. No sharp winged eyeliner, no scowl, no arched villain eyebrows, no realistic doll eyes or detailed eyelashes. Skin and face matte and simply shaded, not shiny.

AGE-APPROPRIATE CUTE COSTUME:
Redesign the original dark-violet/black and dull-gold outfit as a modest little butterfly dress with a fully covered high neckline and torso, a white central front panel, a simple small purple collar jewel, and a rounded knee-length layered skirt. Fully opaque dark-lavender tights and small simple flat ankle boots. No bare midriff, cleavage, thigh-high stockings, garter motifs, high heels or adult hourglass tailoring. Preserve the original silver hair, violet/black paired horns, elf ears, gold edging and butterfly sleeve identity. This is a cute fantasy game character with natural, nonsexual presentation.

BUTTERFLY READABILITY IS ESSENTIAL:
The two large butterfly-shaped sleeves/shawl panels must have unmistakable soft butterfly wings: each side has ONE broad rounded upper-wing lobe and ONE broad smaller rounded lower-wing lobe, with a soft scalloped outer contour rather than leaf spikes or pointed bat wings. They gently open and drape behind/beside her arms so the butterfly outline stays fully visible even in the three-quarter view. Use one large curved lavender and pale-cyan butterfly wing patch per side, smoothly grouped, resembling the butterfly sleeve pattern in image 1. No narrow radiating shards or polygon stripes. Wing panels together form a gentle elegant butterfly silhouette framing her compact body, without becoming actual insect anatomy. Simplify all cloth folds and markings to a few large shapes.
Long silver-white hair falls in 3–4 broad flowing rounded locks; no spiky layered mane. Horns are elegant short upward curved paired violet shapes with gently curved edges and simple large purple inlays; retain pointed tips but avoid aggressive jagged edges. Two broad lower dress/sleeve tails at most.

DELICATE GIRLISH STANDING POSE:
Whole body, face and boots clearly three-quarter toward SCREEN LEFT, around 35–45 degrees. Head has a tiny gentle tilt. Shoulders relaxed and slightly tucked, torso upright. Feet close together with a small natural gap, one foot set just a little behind, knees relaxed; both soles touch the same ground plane. One small hand gently holds the opposite sleeve edge near the lower chest/upper waist, while the other lightly gathers the near butterfly sleeve beside the skirt. Fingers relaxed and softly curved, elbows down. A sweet composed idle standing pose, NOT a battle stance, no claw hand, no fists, no wide squat, no strut, no jumping/floating, no crossed pin-up legs. Keep both hands readable and the sleeve-wing outline unobstructed.

Rendering: same clean simplified hand-painted cartoon as the project references, bold flowing deep violet contours, large solid color masses, 2–3 shades per material, very sparse broad brush strokes. Keep violet/black, silver-white, lavender, cyan and minimal dull-gold palette; soften color transitions into broad painted shapes, never shiny. No dense triangulation, fine jewelry, extra butterflies, sparkles, halo, frame, text, watermark, scenery or props.
Single complete full-body character centered on square canvas, about 84–88 percent total height including horns, generous clear margins around wing tips, horns and feet. Flat uniform warm off-white review background, no paper texture, no checkerboard and no floor shadow.
purpose: User revision: restore butterfly sleeve silhouette, gentle cute youthful chibi appearance and delicate three-quarter left standing pose with project proportions and simplification.
visual_review: Larger rounded head and compact limbs; gentle expression and restrained standing pose facing three-quarter left; visible rounded butterfly sleeve lobes and broad cyan/lavender wing markings; complete silhouette and boots visible; opaque off-white review image.

iterations.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer and pose/proportion correction.
用户最新要求：“比例和简化程度要符合项目角色，3/4战力姿势”。重画图1，必须明显改变头身比、简化密度和站姿，做到可直接与图2和图3放在同一队伍里的角色视觉规格。

Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and identity/costume reference only. Its long adult-fashion body, tiny head, spread arms, floating crossed feet and excessive narrow decorative shapes are precisely what must be changed.
Image 2 (project archer) and image 3 (project hero) are the AUTHORITATIVE BODY-PROPORTION, CARTOON FACE, SIMPLIFICATION and grounded standing references. Match their large head relative to a compact torso, short solid limbs, sturdy feet, clear readable silhouette and economical chunky rendering. Copy neither their clothes, hair, equipment, colors nor sex.
Image 4 is the project's gem icon PAINTING-STYLE reference: strong dark contour, broad simple painted planes, controlled matte purple color, restrained texture.

Create ONE complete full-body female fantasy character with the same silver hair, pointed elf ears, black-violet paired horns, purple eyes, violet butterfly-sleeve robe, small forehead ornament, black-purple costume with simplified dull-gold trim and a white front panel as image 1.

TOP PRIORITY 1 — PROJECT PROPORTIONS:
Use compact approximately THREE-HEAD-TALL body proportions, measuring from the top of the actual head to the soles, EXCLUDING the horn extension. The actual head with face is large, about one-third of that height, just as the archer and hero references. Short torso, shortened thighs and shins, visibly more substantial forearms and boots. A recognizable stylized grown woman in the project's cartoon proportions; do not turn her into a baby. This MUST be a visibly larger head and much shorter legs than image 1. Horns kept as distinctive two curved black-violet points, shortened to suit the compact figure without overwhelming the head.

TOP PRIORITY 2 — CLEAR THREE-QUARTER STANDING READY POSE:
Head, nose, chest, hips, knees and feet all oriented three-quarter toward SCREEN LEFT, approximately 45 degrees from front. Face looks screen-left, not back at viewer. The far eye and far shoulder are visibly narrower/foreshortened. Stable upright battle-idle standing posture, both boot soles planted on the same implied ground plane, feet comfortably apart, front foot slightly toward screen-left, knees only slightly flexed, balanced center of gravity. Front forearm bent gently forward near waist with a small relaxed ready-to-cast open hand; the other hand closer to the body. Elbows low and close, NOT both arms stretched sideways, NOT dancing, NOT walking, NOT floating, NOT jumping, NOT crossed legs or tiptoe. No spell effects or new weapon. Full hands and both feet visible.

TOP PRIORITY 3 — SAME OR SIMPLER DETAIL DENSITY AS PROJECT ARCHER:
Simplify aggressively into a handful of large interlocking shapes. Silver hair grouped into 4–5 thick locks total, one broad back-hair mass. Butterfly sleeves folded downward alongside and slightly behind the torso as 2 large compact draped wing shapes, no giant horizontal display fans. Each visible sleeve gets only one broad lavender/cyan butterfly motif. At most two broad tail panels, no thin looping ribbons or strings. Gold costume trim becomes a few thick clean borders and one central purple ornament. Merge/remove micro chains, tiny diamonds, jewelry clusters and fine ornamentation while keeping the original character recognizable. Use 2–3 main shades per material, very few broad brush planes, strong clean ink-purple outline. Avoid numerous triangular shards, random polygon mosaics, fine hair strands and repeated thin highlights. The eyes are simple project-cartoon violet eyes with a single small highlight, no glossy complex anime eyes.

Keep matte hand-painted cartoon finish with sparse brush texture matching images 2–4; preserve source silver-white / dark violet / lavender / restrained cyan / dull-gold palette. No literal crystalline body or clothing, no jewellery render, no sparkle, no refraction, no realistic skin, no ornate rim, no halo, no badge, no UI, no text or watermark.
Square composition, centered complete character about 86–88 percent of canvas height INCLUDING horns, with clear safe margins all around, plain uniform warm off-white review background, no paper texture, checkerboard, ground shadow or other objects.
Final check before output: the head/body ratio should read like the project hero and archer, with a clear three-quarter LEFT standing silhouette; not like the original tall full-body illustration.
iterations.purpose: User-requested revision to match project character proportions, simplification and three-quarter left standing battle-idle pose.

iterations.prompt:
Redraw the silver-haired horned woman in IMAGE 1 to match EXACTLY the compact body proportions and simplified graphic drawing of the game archer in IMAGE 2. IMAGE 3 is the chunky broad painted color-block reference. This is a structural proportion/simplification correction, not a cosmetic retouch.

The current woman in image 1 remains TOO TALL, TOO SLENDER and TOO FACETED. Required visible changes:
1. Enlarge the actual head and face 35 percent relative to the body, shorten the torso 25 percent, shorten the legs 35 percent, and give the limbs more solid cartoon mass. Match the image 2 archer head-to-body ratio. Approximately THREE real head heights from TOP OF HEAD (excluding horns) to FOOT SOLES. This is a compact cartoon game unit. Do not simply scale the whole existing figure down. Shrink the horn extensions a little so they do not fake the head-size change. Keep her confident grown-woman identity using the project's stylized proportions.
2. Keep a grounded standing battle-idle pose, with both feet firmly planted apart. Rotate the WHOLE FIGURE, including chest, shoulders, pelvis and boots, toward screen-left by 45 degrees, so this is clearly a three-quarter left-facing unit like image 2. Face looks screen-left. Show the far shoulder narrower; avoid a frontal torso with merely a turned head. The forward hand remains small, gently raised with palm ready to cast, rear arm relaxed close to side. Upright, soft knees, no crouching, no floating.
3. Make the painting SIGNIFICANTLY SIMPLER and graphic: head hair = 3 big silver-white masses plus 2 front locks, each with ONE broad lavender shadow. No numerous triangles in hair. Each black/violet clothing panel has one base color and one broad shadow, optional one broad light only. No polygon mosaics, thin repeated slivers, fine scratch texture or shard highlights. Sleeves = two compact draped butterfly-wing masses behind arms, each with ONE simple broad cyan/lavender wing pattern; no radiating many narrow rays. Consolidate gold decoration to collar/shoulder edging, waist line, central purple ornament, simple boot edging. Keep only two broad downward tail panels. The economy of shapes and shading should be equal to or simpler than the archer.
4. Preserve the same female identity, silver-white long hair, violet eyes, two black-purple horns, pointed ears, forehead mark, dark violet butterfly sleeve costume with gold trim and white front panel. Keep the chest/waist/boot design recognizable but simplified. Face should use clear simple cartoon eyes, ONE flat iris color and at most one small white highlight; no delicate anime eyelashes. Preserve a little confident smile.

Bold dark-purple ink contours, matte gouache-like large color blocks with VERY sparse broad brushwork, clear strong silhouette and material separation. NO literal jewel material, shininess, glitter or refractive facets. DO NOT transfer archer's male identity, hair, costume, bow, quiver or colors. One complete full-body woman only. Plain uniform warm off-white background, square canvas, generous clear margins 6–8 percent around all extremities, no props, text, border, shadow, or effects. Her compact silhouette must look ready to stand beside image 2 at the same in-game scale.
